role.altitude: The nuclear medicine radiologist keeps deciding radionuclides and activities, judging whether a request fits, signing prescriptions and teaching residents; typing prescriptions, looking up the indication list and exporting and anonymising teaching cases by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping order sets and the indication list current
role.ambitious_version: A radiologist whose prescriptions and protocol choices start from the department's own standards, and whose teaching file grows while reading.

tasks.short: Decide the radionuclide and activity for the individual patient, enter the prescription, and check and sign it to prescribe radionuclides and dosages.

steps.what: Radiologist decides the radionuclide and activity for the individual patient
Radiologist enters the prescription: radionuclide, activity, route and timing
Radiologist checks the prescription: radionuclide, activity, route and timing against the decision and this patient
Radiologist signs the checked prescription as the named prescriber, releasing it to the radiopharmacy

tasks.design: Deciding the radionuclide and activity stays with the radiologist. The prescription is entered from an order set per protocol in the record, with radionuclide, route and standard activity filled in and the patient's details taken from the record, instead of typing a free order or paper form. The radiologist adjusts the activity where needed and signs as the named prescriber. No software decides a dose.

approvals.approved_version: The prescription with radionuclide, activity, route and timing exactly as checked by the radiologist in s3, signed once for this patient and released to the radiopharmacy; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Prescriptions were typed or written per patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Order sets per protocol in the patient record.
tasks.still_hard: Children and patients with unusual weight or kidney function.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding to lower the activity for a frail patient.
tasks.altitude: Less typing; deciding and signing stay.

evidence.claim: A prescription comes from a named practitioner; software drafts, it does not prescribe.
Order sets in patient records pre-fill standard orders per protocol.

assumptions: Boundary: prescribing; calculating and preparing dosages (task 22734) and obtaining histories (task 17243) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s1: the patient history from task 17243 and the calculated dose from task 22734.
Deciding, checking and signing keep their full time. s2 keeps 50 because the order set fills radionuclide, route, standard activity and patient details, and the radiologist adjusts the activity.
unknowns: Share of prescriptions that follow the standard activity.
research_questions: Do prescription queries from the hot lab fall?

incremental.description: Radiologist keeps order sets in line with protocols.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many activities are non-standard, so half of the order set is overwritten (s2 keeps 75) (7.2); high: mostly standard protocols (14.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive structured procedure requests, check them against the indication list, review procedure requests and medical histories to determine applicability of procedures and radioisotopes, contact the referrer when unsuitable, and record the decision and protocol.

steps.what: Referring clinician fills the structured request form with indication and nuclear medicine questions
Radiologist reads the procedure request and checks it against the department's indication list
Radiologist reviews the medical history to determine applicability of the procedure and radioisotopes
Radiologist contacts the referrer when the procedure does not fit
Radiologist records the decision and the chosen protocol and radioisotope

tasks.design: The request form asks the referrer for the indication from a fixed list and for pregnancy, breastfeeding, recent iodine contrast and interfering medication. Rules match the indication to the department's list and show the usual protocol and radioisotope, so the radiologist does not look them up in the protocol book. Reviewing the history and deciding applicability stay with the radiologist. The radiologist records the decision as today and picks the protocol shown by the rules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were free text and the indication list was a separate document.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured request forms and rule-based protocol matching.
tasks.still_hard: Requests with unusual or vague indications.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that another scan answers the question better.

reach.learn: Whether structured requests are refused less often.

evidence.claim: Structured requests with indication lists are configured in imaging request systems.
Decision software is usually a medical device; rule matching here only shows the department's own list.

assumptions: Boundary: judging applicability; obtaining histories (task 17243) and advising physicians on indications (task 22733) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3: the patient history obtained under task 17243.
The referrer's extra fields are shown in s1 and take about as long as the free text they replace.

Reviewing, deciding and contacting keep their full time. s2 keeps 60 because the rules match the indication instead of a look-up in the protocol book; s5 keeps 85 because only finding the protocol goes and the decision is written as today.
unknowns: Share of requests with a listed indication.
research_questions: Do unsuitable requests reach the scanner less often?

incremental.description: Radiologist keeps the indication list and protocol mapping current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many requests arrive in free text outside the list (s2 keeps 85, s5 keeps 95) (4.5); high: most requests with listed indications (13.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and anonymise teaching cases, prepare slides and questions, teach nuclear medicine or diagnostic radiology at graduate level, and assess residents' progress.

steps.what: Radiologist selects and anonymises teaching cases from the image archive
Radiologist teaches nuclear medicine or diagnostic radiology to residents at the workstation and in lectures

tasks.design: While reading, the radiologist flags interesting studies to a teaching file in the image archive, which exports them with patient identifiers removed, instead of exporting and anonymising each case by hand before a lecture. Slides use a template that takes images from the teaching file. Teaching and assessing residents stay with the radiologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cases were exported and anonymised one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Teaching files in the image archive with anonymised export.
tasks.still_hard: Burned-in patient names on older images.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a resident how to look, not only what to see.

reach.learn: Whether a larger case library helps learning.

evidence.claim: Image archives offer teaching files with anonymised export.

assumptions: Boundary: graduate teaching; instructing radiologic staff (task 17246) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: studies flagged to the teaching file while reading under task 17254.
Teaching and assessing keep their full time.
research_questions: Does preparation time per lecture fall?

incremental.description: Radiologist checks anonymised exports for burned-in names.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few studies are flagged while reading, so most cases are still found and anonymised by hand (s1 keeps 80) and slides gain little (s2 keeps 95) (5.7); high: a growing teaching file (16.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
